observed: The current structured parser AST has first-class Module.name and Module.uses.
The current ClayExecutableTypedIR/v1 materializer does not emit module name or use declarations; it emits provenance hashes plus reachable executable functions.
The current grammar distinguishes bare use qid from use qid.* but syntax lowering stores only _text(kids[0]), so wildcard-vs-bare form is not explicitly preserved in Module.uses.

A legacy/current-tree WP04 module_symbol_resolver candidate exists and builds deterministic fail-closed module/symbol environments, but reparses source with regex rather than consuming the canonical structured AST.
dependency_trust.py builds a content-addressed transitive module closure on top of that resolver and explicitly grants no trust by itself.
Minimal clayenv is provenance-strict but remains single-source and has no canonical package/module resolution path.
hypothesis: The smallest safe path to a canonical package/module system is to make use declarations lossless in the canonical AST, carry module/import identity through canonical executable/build metadata, then migrate the existing deterministic resolver/closure algorithm to consume those canonical structures instead of reparsing source.
counterhypothesis: The legacy regex resolver could be wired directly into clayenv as a host-side package layer without changing executable semantics.
counterhypothesis_rejection_reason: That would create a second source parser/semantic boundary beside the current parser/analyzer/TypedIR path and risks divergence between build semantics and package resolution.
discriminating_next_tests: Parser gate: prove bare use and wildcard use remain distinguishable after canonical AST lowering.
Resolver equivalence gate: on the existing 40-source corpus, compare legacy resolver environments to an AST-consuming resolver where both are defined; preserve disagreements as counterevidence.
Duplicate-module gate: two files claiming the same canonical module identity must fail closed before artifact admission.
Closure provenance gate: changing any transitive imported source must change the dependency closure identity and the ClayEnv build identity.
Relocation control: moving an unchanged package root must not change semantic package identity.

bounded_unusual_experiment.name: ghost-module twin
bounded_unusual_experiment.variant: same executable body with module renamed to clay.beta
bounded_unusual_experiment.result: Source/provenance hash changes, while the non-provenance executable payload shape is identical and has no explicit module identity.
bounded_unusual_experiment.interpretation: Current provenance detects the rename but does not constitute a first-class executable module identity or resolver contract.
bounded_unusual_experiment.rollback: No repository/product mutation was performed by the experiment.

architecture_delta.decision: Do not wire the regex resolver directly into clayenv. First make canonical use/module identity lossless, then fuse the resolver/closure algorithm onto that boundary.
